Refresh policies control how and when a materialized {C.CAGG} catches up with its source {C.HYPERTABLE}. You can run refreshes on a schedule or trigger them manually when you need a one-off catch-up.

## Prerequisites

<PrereqCloudSelf />

## Change the refresh policy

{C.CAGG_CAP}s require a policy for automatic refreshing. You can adjust
this to suit different use cases. For example, you can have the {C.CAGG}
and the {C.HYPERTABLE} stay in sync, even when data is removed from the
{C.HYPERTABLE}. Alternatively, you could keep source data in the {C.CAGG} even after
it is removed from the {C.HYPERTABLE}.

You can change the way your {C.CAGG} is refreshed by calling
`add_continuous_aggregate_policy`.

Among others, `add_continuous_aggregate_policy` takes the following arguments:

- `start_offset`: the start of the refresh window relative to when the policy
  runs
- `end_offset`: the end of the refresh window relative to when the policy runs
- `schedule_interval`: the refresh interval in minutes or hours. Defaults to
  24 hours.

Note the following:

- If you set the `start_offset` or `end_offset` to `NULL`, the range is open-ended and extends to the beginning or end of time.
- If you set `end_offset` within the current {C.TIME_BUCKET}, this bucket is excluded from materialization. This is done for the following reasons:

  - The current bucket is incomplete and can't be refreshed.
  - The current bucket gets a lot of writes in the timestamp order, and its aggregate becomes outdated very quickly. Excluding it improves performance.

  To include the latest raw data in queries, enable [{C.RTAGG}](/build/continuous-aggregates/real-time-aggregates).

See the [API reference](/reference/timescaledb/continuous-aggregates/add_continuous_aggregate_policy) for the full list of required and optional arguments and use examples.

The policy in the following example ensures that all data in the {C.CAGG} is up to date with the {C.HYPERTABLE}, except for data written within the last hour of wall-clock time. The policy also does not refresh the last {C.TIME_BUCKET} of the {C.CAGG}.

Since the policy in this example runs once every hour (`schedule_interval`) while also excluding data within the most recent hour (`end_offset`), it takes up to 2 hours for data written to the {C.HYPERTABLE} to be reflected in the {C.CAGG}. Backfills, which are usually outside the most recent hour of data, will be visible after up to 1 hour depending on when the policy last ran when the data was written.

Because it has an open-ended `start_offset` parameter, any data that is removed
from the table, for example with a `DELETE` or with `drop_chunks`, is also removed
from the {C.CAGG} view. This means that the {C.CAGG}
always reflects the data in the underlying {C.HYPERTABLE}.

To change a refresh policy to use a `NULL` `start_offset`:

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title={`Connect to your ${C.SERVICE_LONG}`}>
In <a href={C.CONSOLE_URL}>{C.CONSOLE}</a> open an SQL editor. You can also connect to your {C.SERVICE_SHORT} using psql.
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Create the refresh policy">
Create a new policy on `conditions_summary_hourly` that keeps the {C.CAGG} up to date, and runs every hour:

```sql
SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy('conditions_summary_hourly',
  start_offset => NULL,
  end_offset => INTERVAL '1 h',
  schedule_interval => INTERVAL '1 h');
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

If you want to keep data in the {C.CAGG} even if it is removed from
the underlying {C.HYPERTABLE}, you can set the `start_offset` to match the
[data retention policy](/learn/data-management/data-retention) on the source {C.HYPERTABLE}. For example,
if you have a retention policy that removes data older than one month, set
`start_offset` to one month or less. This sets your policy so that it does not
refresh the dropped data.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title={`Connect to your ${C.SERVICE_LONG}`}>
In <a href={C.CONSOLE_URL}>{C.CONSOLE}</a> open an SQL editor. You can also connect to your {C.SERVICE_SHORT} using psql.
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Create the refresh policy">
Create a new policy on `conditions_summary_hourly`
that keeps data removed from the {C.HYPERTABLE} in the {C.CAGG}, and
runs every hour:

```sql
SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy('conditions_summary_hourly',
  start_offset => INTERVAL '1 month',
  end_offset => INTERVAL '1 h',
  schedule_interval => INTERVAL '1 h');
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

<Callout variant="note">
It is important to consider your data retention policies when you're setting up
{C.CAGG} policies. If the {C.CAGG} policy window covers
data that is removed by the data retention policy, the data will be removed when
the aggregates for those buckets are refreshed. For example, if you have a data
retention policy that removes all data older than two weeks, the {C.CAGG}
policy will only have data for the last two weeks.
</Callout>

## Add concurrent refresh policies

You can add concurrent refresh policies on each {C.CAGG}, as long as their
start and end offsets don't overlap. For example, to backfill data into older {C.CHUNK}s you
set up one policy that refreshes recent data, and another that refreshes backfilled data.

The first policy in this example keeps the {C.CAGG} up to date with data that was
inserted in the past day. Any data that was inserted or updated for previous days is refreshed by
the second policy.

<NumberedList>
<NumberedItem title={`Connect to your ${C.SERVICE_LONG}`}>
In <a href={C.CONSOLE_URL}>{C.CONSOLE}</a> open an SQL editor. You can also connect to your {C.SERVICE_SHORT} using psql.
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Create the recent data policy">
Create a new policy on `conditions_summary_daily`
to refresh the {C.CAGG} with recently inserted data which runs
hourly:

```sql
SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy('conditions_summary_daily',
  start_offset => INTERVAL '1 day',
  end_offset => INTERVAL '1 h',
  schedule_interval => INTERVAL '1 h');
```
</NumberedItem>

<NumberedItem title="Create the backfill policy">
Create a concurrent policy on `conditions_summary_daily` to refresh the {C.CAGG} with
backfilled data:

```sql
SELECT add_continuous_aggregate_policy('conditions_summary_daily',
  start_offset => NULL,
  end_offset => INTERVAL '1 day',
  schedule_interval => INTERVAL '1 hour');
```
</NumberedItem>
</NumberedList>

## Manually refresh a {C.CAGG}

If you need to manually refresh a {C.CAGG}, you can use the
`refresh` command. This recomputes the data within the window that has changed
in the underlying {C.HYPERTABLE} since the last refresh. Therefore, if only a few
buckets need updating, the refresh runs quickly.

If you have recently dropped data from a {C.HYPERTABLE} with a {C.CAGG},
calling `refresh_continuous_aggregate` on a region containing dropped {C.CHUNK}s
recalculates the aggregate without the dropped data. See
[drop data](/build/continuous-aggregates/drop-data) for more information.

The `refresh` command takes three arguments:

- The name of the {C.CAGG} view to refresh
- The timestamp of the beginning of the refresh window
- The timestamp of the end of the refresh window

Only buckets that are wholly within the specified range are refreshed. For
example, if you specify `2021-05-01', '2021-06-01` the only buckets that are
refreshed are those up to but not including 2021-06-01. It is possible to
specify `NULL` in a manual refresh to get an open-ended range, but we do not
recommend using it, because you could inadvertently materialize a large amount
of data, slow down your performance, and have unintended consequences on other
policies like data retention.

To manually refresh a {C.CAGG}, use the `refresh` command:

```sql
CALL refresh_continuous_aggregate('example', '2021-05-01', '2021-06-01');
```

Follow the logic used by automated refresh policies and avoid refreshing {C.TIME_BUCKET}s that are likely to have a lot of writes. This means that you should generally not refresh the latest incomplete {C.TIME_BUCKET}. To include the latest raw data in your queries, use [{C.RTAGG}](/build/continuous-aggregates/real-time-aggregates) instead.
